primitives.name: Kick frequency reduction
primitives.verbatim_quote: FOOT-BALL IN AMERICA 107 Mass and wedge plays have been very much curtailed, and with design, by the insistence upon more kicking.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes standard American football ruleset emphasizing kicking over mass formations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down into pure kicking strategies when rule enforcement is absolute.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Models the strategic shift from mass plays to kicking frequency as a decision-theoretic optimization under rule constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Observed decrease in wedge formation frequency relative to kicking plays.

primitives.name: Wedge play curtailment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Every kick-off and free kick had come to be the signal for a wedge.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes pre-rule-change dominance of wedges triggered by all kicks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates to zero wedge usage when kicking becomes rare.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Treats wedge curtailment as a Bayesian updating problem where new rules revise prior probabilities of wedge formation.
layer2.telemetry: Historical data on wedge occurrence rates before and after rule changes.

primitives.name: Kicking scarcity
primitives.verbatim_quote: Now, thanks to the rules, they can be used but seldom.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rules limit total number of kicking opportunities per game.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Approaches zero kicking when rules become extremely restrictive.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Maps kicking scarcity to a conformal prediction interval for feasible kicking events given current constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of actual kicks to theoretically maximum possible kicks per season.

primitives.assumptions: Assumes a sequential decision tree where runs are primary options unless kicking is forced.

These operators collectively form a closed-loop system: reduced kicking leads to fewer wedges, which forces more runs, which in turn influences future kicking decisions. The resulting dynamics create feedback loops that stabilize around a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium.
